title: Plants and Animals
seo_title: Kindergarten Science: Plants and Animals Worksheets (BC Curriculum)
standard_text: Plants and animals have observable features: basic needs (food, water, shelter, space), features of local plants (roots, stems, leaves, flowers, seeds) and animals (shape, size, feet, teeth, body covering), and First Peoples knowledge of local plants and animals. (summary of BC's Curriculum, Science K, Biology)
meta_desc: Free Kindergarten science worksheets (BC): parts of plants and animals, what living things need, and homes and habitats. 100 picture questions with answers.
key_big: Living things need food, water, a home.
key_sub: Look at the parts: leaves and roots, legs and fur.
body_html:
How to think about it

Plants and animals have parts that help them live.

  • Plants have roots, stems, leaves and flowers.
  • Animals have legs, fins, wings, fur or feathers.
  • All living things need food, water and a safe home.
Example

What does a plant need to grow?

Think of what a plant drinks and what shines on it.

Answer: water and sunlight

Example

Which animal has feathers?

Feathers cover birds.

Answer: a bird

Common mistakes

  • Saying a plant eats food like an animal.
  • Thinking fish have fur.

faq.q: Why do animals need a home?
faq.a: A home keeps them safe and gives them shelter from rain and cold.
Roots hold the plant in the ground and take in water.

items.q: A basil plant is kept in the fridge. What will happen?
c: It is too hot, so it dries out and wilts.
It has warmth and light, so it grows well.
It is too cold, so it stops growing and goes black.
Nothing happens, because cold is good for plants.
items.e: Plants need a suitable temperature: not too hot and not too cold.
